scope: Independent static visual QA only; no clinical, biomechanical or motion certification
decisionRule: Only concrete important defects require regeneration; small margins without physical crops are documented rather than rejected.

items.identification: Standing cable press identification is plausible from lateral anchor and hands held together in front of torso.
observations: Cable is one continuous segment from pulley connection to handle, without split or duplicate segment.
Cable overlaps upper arms in the image plane, but remains visibly continuous in front; this view does not establish an actual body penetration.
Hands and forearms overlap strongly in perspective; individual grips cannot be fully assessed.
Full body and complete tower, overhead attachment and base feet visible.
limitations: Oblique camera view makes exact transverse alignment of torso relative to anchor ambiguous. Do not use this still to certify anti-rotation technique.
